text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Thirty civilians massacred in Chebli, south of Algiers.

- The interior ministry warns "for the last time" political parties to change manifestos in line with a party law. The warning came ahead of an April 21 deadline on candidates to register for the June 5 legislative elections. The ministry did not say which parties still have to rename themselves.

- The interior ministry says Islamist Hamas party leader Mahfoud Nahnah allegations were baseless. Nahnah said on Sunday the ministry drive to force his party to change name was unconstitutional. Hamas has changed its name.
- Thirty civilians slaughtered by "terrorists" in Chebli.
- Security forces kill seven "terrorists" at Jolie Vue suburb, in Algiers.

- Algeria's former president Ahmed Ben Bella said he is a Moroccan citizen. He said his mother and father are from the Moroccan city of Marrakesh. Ben Bella was speaking at a Madrid meeting with other Algerian opponents who urged the Algerian government to negotiate a political solution with radical Islamists to end bloodshed.
